append.text: **Ps 55:2–3 *conculcávit me homo … Conculcavérunt me* → *me calcou aos pés … Calcaram-me aos pés*** — draft 1 had the proposed *pisar aos pés*; the Ps 55 stylist refused it in both verses as two idioms crossed and asked for *calcar aos pés*, the set phrase (= 90:13, MS1932). Taken: Ps 7's readers stumbled on the rare subjunctive *calque*, not on the idiom. Proposal for the row: *calcar aos pés*, with Ps 7:6's *pise aos pés* as the one local exception (subjunctive). Passed the Latinist gate.
Ps 55:2 *tribulávit me* → *me atribulou* — unknown to the blind reader again (the fourth psalm); kept.
**Ps 55:7 *ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt* → *eles espreitarão o meu calcanhar*** — the row applied; unknown to the blind reader again (the second psalm); passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 55:4 *Ab altitúdine diéi timébo* → *Da altura do dia temerei*** — the concrete word kept at the crux (noon, or height as pride); the Latinist (v1) asked plain *da* for draft 1's *desde*, which made *ab* only temporal. MS1932 *desde que desponta o dia* refused. The blind reader listed *altura do dia* as unclear — the Latin's own obscurity.

**Ps 55:8 *Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam* → *Assim como esperaram pela minha alma*** — the enemies lying in wait: the row's verb kept with a hostile subject (ὑπέμειναν); the blind reader did not hear the hostility at once (options *aguardaram*, *vida*); passed the Latinist twice.
**Ps 55:9b *tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum* → *então os meus inimigos voltarão para trás*** — as this row foresaw; heard as retreat.

**Ps 55:12 *vota tua, quæ reddam* → *os vossos votos, que pagarei*** — the row held (decision `reddam`); the stylist found *pagar votos* commercial and asked *cumprir* (MS1932) — refused for the formula's six places, an option.

**Ps 55:13 *eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu* → *arrancastes a minha alma da morte, e os meus pés da queda*** — sources named, so *arrancar*; no reader remarked. **114:8** (*erípuit ánimam meam de morte … pedes meos a lapsu*) should copy it.

**Ps 55:9 *posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo* → *pusestes as minhas lágrimas à vossa vista*** (the Wednesday Matins versicle's response); *à vista de* applied; the stylist named 55:9 the psalm's best line.

**Ps 55:11 decides locally, as D15 asked: *In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem* → *Em Deus louvarei a palavra, no Senhor louvarei a fala*.** Draft 1's *a palavra … a palavra* was refused by both the Latinist (minor) and the stylist (worst line: 'sounds like a copying slip'); the Greek differs here too (ῥῆμα / λόγον), D15's own test. *a fala* (the stylist's) over *o discurso* (the Latinist's, heard as an oration). 55:5 *sermónes meos* and 55:6 *verba mea* (both τοὺς λόγους μου) stay *as minhas palavras*; the v2 gate asked *falas* at 55:5 (minor) — refused under D15. So *sermo* is *palavra* and *fala* in one psalm: for whoever rules.

terms: | bellári | guerrear (*os que guerreiam contra mim*) | open | Ps 55:3 only (grep); πολεμέω, the same Greek as 55:2 *impúgnans* → *combater*, but the Latin varies and *guerrear* keeps *bellum* (17:40 → *guerra*); *lutar*, *combater*, *pelejam* (MS1932) options. No reader remarked. |

| exsecrári | detestar (*detestavam as minhas palavras*) | open | Ps 55:6 (the noun *exsecrátio* 58:13 — grep). L&S 'curse, execrate'; the Greek ἐβδελύσσοντο 'abhorred'; *abominar* is abominári's (5:7b, 118:163). DRB 'detested'. Options *execrar*, *amaldiçoar*. No reader remarked; 58:13's noun decides for itself. |
| promíssio | promessa | open | Ps 55:9b only (grep; ἐπαγγελία). *Assim como também na vossa promessa* — the ellipsis kept; the blind reader found it incomplete, as the Latin is. |
| lapsus | queda (*os meus pés da queda*) | open | Ps 55:13, 114:8 (grep; ὀλίσθημα, a slip). MS1932. Heard as falling into sin first; 114:8 should copy. |

| pro níhilo (55:8 *pro níhilo salvos fácies illos*) | por nada | open | Ps 55:8 (ὑπὲρ τοῦ μηθενὸς); DRB 'for nothing'. The blind reader heard it split between 'in no way' and 'freely' — the Latin's openness; MS1932 *de nenhum modo* decides (option). 80:15, 89:5, 105:24 are other builds (*pro níhilo habére*) and decide locally. |

| abscóndere without an object (55:7 *Inhabitábunt et abscóndent*) | *esconderão* (bare) | open | Ps 55:7 (κατακρύψουσιν, no object). Draft 1's reflexive *se esconderão* (DRB, MS1932) was marked by the Latinist (minor) as changing the voice; the bare verb taken, and he passed it at the gate. *inhabitáre → habitar* (36:29). |

| placére coram (55:13 *ut pláceam coram Deo*) | agradar diante de (*para que eu agrade diante de Deus*) | open | Ps 55:13 (εὐαρεστῆσαι ἐνώπιον); keeps *coram*; MS1932 *seja agradável a Deus* drops it (option *seja agradável*). Cf. the row placére + dative (52:6b, 114:9). No reader remarked. |

| cognóscere + *quóniam* (55:10 *ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es*) | *eis que eu soube: vós sois o meu Deus* | open | Ps 55:10 v2: the stylist found *conheci que* not current and the bare *eis,* clipped; the perfect kept as 19:7a (*agora soube*). The v2 gate (minor) asked back *eis que conheci que vós sois* — held (option): he called both defensible. |
formulas: | *In Deo laudábo sermónes meos / verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: in Deo sperávi: non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro / homo* (55:5 ≈ 55:11, the refrain; 55:11 in the Gradual of Quad3-1 with *sperábo*) | 55:5 *Em Deus louvarei as minhas palavras, em Deus esperei: * não temerei o que me faça a carne*; 55:11 *Em Deus louvarei a palavra, no Senhor louvarei a fala: * em Deus esperei, não temerei o que me faça o homem* | open — Ps 55; *não temerei o que me faça o homem* = 117:6 word for word (rule 6); the two verses differ only where the Latin does |

| *V. Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi. R. Posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo* (55:9; the Wednesday Matins versicle, Psalmi matutinum [Daya3]; Quad5-5; Tract of Quad3-1) | *Deus, eu vos anunciei a minha vida. R. Pusestes as minhas lágrimas à vossa vista* | open — Ps 55; each colon reads alone; the stylist's best line |

| *Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: tota die impúgnans (bellans) tribulávit me* (55:2; Gradual/Tract of Quad3-1 and Quad5-1 with *bellans*, grep) | *Tende piedade de mim, Deus, porque o homem me calcou aos pés: * o dia todo, combatendo, me atribulou* | open — Ps 55 |
